summary: NO-SHIP. R2-F001 and R2-F003 are fixed, and the pure classifier corpus plus syntax checks pass. However, one HIGH classifier bypass remains, and R2-F002 only partially hardens the audit path. I could not run the complete break-glass validator because this sandbox prohibits the temporary filesystem writes it requires; that limitation was not itself scored as a failure.

findings.claim: Clustered ripgrep short options bypass the read-only classifier's subprocess restriction.
findings.analysis: isSafeRg rejects only the exact token `-z`. Ripgrep permits clustered short options, so `rg -iz needle archive.gz` enables `-z/--search-zip` while isReadOnlyTool returns true. Ripgrep implements this mode by launching decompressor processes, defeating the classifier's explicit attempt to prevent subprocess-capable flags. The same boundary also trusts ambient RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH configuration, which can inject `--pre` unless `--no-config` is enforced.
evidence: hooks/codex/lib/codex-hook-context.mjs:216-223 rejects `token === "-z"` but does not inspect short-option clusters.
Direct pure-classifier probe: `isReadOnlyTool("rg -iz needle archive.gz")` returned true.
Local ripgrep probe accepted `-iz` as valid clustered options: exit 1 for no match versus exit 2 for an invalid option.
The official [ripgrep FAQ](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/blob/master/FAQ.md) states that `-z/--search-zip` shells out to decompressor binaries.

The official [ripgrep guide](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/blob/master/GUIDE.md) states that configuration arguments are prepended from RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH and recommends `--no-config` to prevent them.
findings.proposed_fix: Parse ripgrep short-option clusters and reject any cluster containing `z`; add `rg -iz` and `rg -nz` denial vectors. Also refuse read-only classification when RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH is active unless the invocation contains `--no-config`.

findings.claim: The audit trail can still retain insecure permissions or be redirected through a symlinked parent directory.
findings.analysis: O_NOFOLLOW protects only the final audit filename. The env-form break-glass returns before validating `~/.svc`, and breakGlassAllow then uses recursive mkdir plus a pathname open, so an existing `~/.svc` directory symlink can redirect the audit silently. Additionally, the 0600 mode passed to openSync applies only when creating a file; an existing same-owner 0666 or legacy 0644 audit file is accepted without rejection or correction. This leaves integrity or confidentiality dependent on pre-existing mode.
evidence: bin/svc-enforce.mjs:73-74 arms the env form before any state-directory validation.
bin/svc-enforce.mjs:101-112 does not lstat or securely validate the audit directory before opening its child path.
bin/svc-enforce.mjs:108-110 validates audit type and owner but not mode.
The validator tests a symlinked final audit filename, but not a symlinked `.svc` parent or a permissive pre-existing audit file.
findings.proposed_fix: Validate `~/.svc` as a real same-UID, non-group/other-writable directory for both break-glass forms. After opening, fstat the descriptor and require a regular same-UID file; reject or fchmod pre-existing files to 0600. Add parent-symlink and pre-existing-0666 regression cases.
